column3: Every Sunday, Little Red Riding Hood brought her grandma a cake. And every Sunday, the big bad wolf got a little bit fatter.
At first, nobody noticed. I mean, wolves eat a lot, right?
But after a month, the wolf couldn't fit through the door of his own cave.
Red got suspicious. Grandma said she loved the cakes. But grandma never got any bigger.
So Red asks the hunter for help.
The hunter looks at the wolf. Then at Red. And goes: so your problem is a fat wolf?
He laughs all the way back into the forest.
So one night, Red hides in grandma's closet. And waits.
Three a.m. The front door creaks open.
The wolf squeezes inside. And grandma is already waiting for him. With a fork.
But she doesn't take a single bite. She feeds him. Every crumb. Every single cake.
Because grandma knew exactly how dangerous that wolf was.
And a wolf this fat can't chase anyone.
For five years, grandma hasn't eaten a single piece of cake.
And Red Riding Hood? Has never been safer.
